selection: USGS M>=7.0 events 2000-01-01..2026-10-19 with >= 365 days of prior data and 90 days of follow-up; events within the Wells-Coppersmith rupture-length radius, M>=4.5 (the downloaded catalogue). Fit starts 0.25 d after the mainshock.

out_of_sample_30_to_90_days.metric_note: |log((observed+1)/(predicted+1))|; 0 is perfect. Coverage ignores parameter uncertainty.

methods.poisson_plugin: Poisson quantiles around the fitted expected count (parameters treated as exact).
methods.parameter_uncertainty: Parametric simulation: 4000 draws of (log K, [log c], p) from the MLE's normal approximation (inverse Hessian), Poisson count per draw; nothing is tuned on the evaluated sequences.
methods.parameter_uncertainty_nb: As parameter_uncertainty, but the count per draw is negative binomial with Var = lam + d * lam^2; d is fitted by maximum likelihood (mixture over the parameter draws) on mainshocks before 2013 only.

predictive_intervals.note: poisson_plugin and parameter_uncertainty use only each sequence's own 0.25-30 day fit, so every sequence is out of sample. parameter_uncertainty_nb borrows d from mainshocks before 2013: only the mainshocks_2013_and_later rows are out of sample for it (the earlier rows are in-sample and shown for comparison).

limitations: M4.5+ global catalogue: only the largest aftershocks are seen, and early aftershocks are missing while the mainshock coda masks them.
Radius from rupture-length scaling is a heuristic; nearby independent activity is included.
Sequences with a larger later event were excluded, which favours simple sequences.
This evaluation is offline; the application never extrapolates fits beyond the data.
